translation: Bitter can dry dampness and harden; fire is bitter. The Yi (《易》) says: Among things that dry the ten thousand things, none is more scorching than fire; all things, when dried, become hard. Sweet can relax urgency and disperse binding; sweet is earth. Dryness can make urgency bind; therefore relaxing makes the urgent disperse. Acrid can disperse depression, disperse binding, and moisten dryness; acrid is metal. Metal governs scattering and falling, and metal generates water—this is the reason. Moreover, when depression and binding are dispersed, then qi and fluids circulate freely, and fluids (津液) are generated.
translator_notes: 津液 rendered 'fluids'; 抑結散 rendered 'depression and binding are dispersed'.
